Saudi Aramco also cut December prices across all grades for Northwest Europe and the Mediterranean by $1 a barrel

Reuters News

SINGAPORE - Saudi Aramco cut its December price for its Arab Light grade for Asian customers by $2 a barrel versus November on Friday, to a discount of $6.50 a barrel to the Oman/Dubai average, the lowest since May 2020 during the pandemic.

The producer also cut December prices across all grades for Northwest Europe and the Mediterranean by $1 a barrel while keeping prices unchanged in the US, a pricing document showed.

Market participants were expecting Aramco to keep prices for Asia unchanged or cut by up to $2 a barrel to entice buyers due to ample Middle East supplies and weaker spot market premiums, according to a Reuters survey last week.

Spot premiums for Middle Eastern crude benchmarks returned to levels seen before the US-Israeli war on Iran this week as producers ramped up exports despite rising attacks on tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz, while cooling refining margins in Asia slowed buying interest.

HSBC raised its fourth-quarter crude production forecast for Saudi Arabia to 8.3 million bpd from 6.3 million bpd, citing a faster-than-expected export recovery.

The bank raised its 2027 production forecast to 9.8 million bpd from 8.8 million bpd and said it expects output to return to about 10 million bpd by mid-2027.

(Reporting by Florence Tan and Siyi Liu; Editing by Jacqueline Wong and Thomas Derpinghaus)
